html:
Italy is one of the favorite destinations for students around the world with its historical texture, cultural wealth and rooted educational institutions. The wide range of programs it offers especially for master's education and the relatively affordable living costs have become an attractive option for many Turkish students. But while studying abroad, financial support comes to the top of the topics students are most interested and researched. In this context, the credit and scholarship opportunities provided by the Credit and Household Institution of the Ministry of Youth and Sports of the Republic of Turkey (KYK) can be an important source of support for students considering to take a master's degree in Italy. In this blog post, when you are graduated in Italy The Italian Loan And we will discuss in detail how you can benefit from the scholarship, application and renewal processes.

Requirements for a Master's degree in Italy

Students who are a citizen of the Republic of Turkey and who have graduated abroad may also benefit from KYK credit or scholarship if they provide specific requirements. However, there are some differences and additional procedures compared to domestic applications.

General Request Conditions

  • Being a citizen of the Republic: It is essential to be a citizen of the Republic of Turkey to benefit from the credit and scholarship.

  • Being a Master Student: In an institution of higher education in Italy (university, academy, etc.) Master You need to be registered in the program. Doctoral students can also be included in this coverage.

  • Providing a specific criterion of success (for burses): Academic success in scholarship applications is an important criterion. The credit application does not require success.

  • The physical situation: The financial status of the student and his family is assessed in the scholarship applications. In terms of credit, this criterion is more flexible.

  • Not to stay outside: Having previously received a scholarship or loan from KYK and not cut off for reasons such as failure, disciplinary crime.

Special Foreign Education Conditions

One of the most important requirements for students studying abroad is the program studied by the Higher Education Council in Turkey (YÖK) The equality to carry. The master's programs of most universities in Italy provide this equality requirement. However, it is important that students confirm the equality of YÖK for their own programs before applying.

Also, there are specific documents and special procedures that students studying abroad need to submit to the KYK. This procedure will be taken through the foreign representations of Turkey in Italy (Ambassy or Consulate Education Office). Special Student Certificate is coming.

Application process and necessary documents

Applications are usually every year. October-November This is done through the e-Government. However, students studying abroad need to follow different steps in the application process.

Application steps

  1. Application for the e-Government: Following the official announcement of KYK, fill out the online application form via e-Government on the specified dates. In this form you need to specify your educational information, personal information and the income status of your family in a correct and complete manner.

  2. Preparation of the necessary documents: After completing your application, you will need to prepare the documents that the system will request from you. For students who study abroad, these documents include Student Certificate It takes great importance.

List of documents required (for abroad)

  • Copy of the wallet: It is necessary to verify your identity information.

  • Students from the foreign country: This document is the official document that you will receive from your university in Italy and confirms that you are a student. The document must include the name of the program you study, start and end dates, information such as your student number. This document The Apostle You may have to be approved by the representation of Turkey in Italy.

  • Special Student Certificate (approved by Attestation): This document has a critical importance for foreign students. This document you need to get from the Turkish Education Department in Italy officially declares that you are a "special student" studying abroad. It is detailed how this document will be obtained.

  • The transcript (license ) : A score that shows your academic success in your bachelor's education. Burs is more important for applications.

  • Income status documents: Documents such as salary borders that show your family’s income, tapu records, vehicle licenses. These documents are used to evaluate, especially in scholarship applications.

  • Registration of the Court: It can be taken through the e-government.

  • The Certificate of Residence: It can be taken through the e-government.

The important note: All documents must be up-to-date and complete. If the documents are in Italian, it may be requested by the sworn translator to be translated into Turkish and notary approved.

Special Student Certificate and Attachment Processes

Higher degree in Italy The Italian Loan or one of the most critical steps to get a scholarship, you need to take from the Education Department of Turkey in Italy Special Student Certificateto be. This document ensures that your KYK application is assessed in the category of foreign students.

How to obtain a special student certificate?

  1. The Turkish Education Department in Italy: First, you should contact the Education Department within the Romanian Embassy or the General Consulate of Milan. You may need to get a date on the website or by phone.

  2. Preparing the necessary documents: Attachment will ask you for the following documents to prepare a private student certificate:

* Copy of the passport: Certificate of identity and citizenship. * Photocopy of the Student Visa: It shows you are legally in Italy. * Current Student Certificate obtained from the University in Italy: You will receive from your university the formal and signed/closed Student Certificate. The information in this document, such as the study time, start and end dates, program name, must be complete. * Letter of acceptance: A copy of the admission letter you received from the university. Diploma and Transcript: Documents that show you have completed your bachelor's education. * Certificate of residence (Permesso di Soggiorno): Document that shows your legal residence permit in Italy. If you don’t have Permesso di Soggiorno yet, you can submit the application certificate. * The request: A special student certificate requiring your application.

  1. Applications for the Appeal: With the documents you have prepared, you may need to apply personally or send them by mail. The staff will review your documents and evaluate your request and, if appropriate, prepare your special student document.

  2. Presentation of the document to KYK: The special student certificate you receive must be delivered to the University of New Orleans along with other documents requested by the University of New Orleans in the specified manner (usually by e-Government or by post) to the University of New Orleans.

The important warning: Doctors are carefully examining the documents. Student Certificate Since it is one of the most important documents in the process, make sure that the document you will receive from your university has all the formalities. In some cases, more detailed and formal documents may be required instead of simple student documents issued by universities. According to the experience that a student has experienced, there have been cases where the document in the PDF format received from the university system is not sufficient, an original document with the university seal and signature is required. Therefore, it is most accurate to know the current document requests by contacting the Office in advance.

Renewal of the loan step by step

Students who receive a KYK scholarship or credit must renew these supports at a specific date each year. The renewal The process requires the presentation of a special student certificate and current student certificate in the same way for foreign students.

The steps of renewal

  1. Follow the announcement: Each year, the KYK announces credit/burs renewal dates and necessary documents via the official website. It is important to follow these reports regularly.

  2. Get the current student certificate: A current show that you are registered for the new academic year from your university in Italy Student Certificate Take it. This document must be formal and detailed as the previous year.

  3. New Special Student Certificate: In the process of renewal, KYK will also ask you for a current special student certificate. Therefore, you need to obtain a new private student certificate from the Education Department in Italy by following the steps described above.

  4. Deliver the documents to KYK: Send the current student certificate and the new private student certificate you get to the KYK by the method specified by the KYK (usually e-Government or mail). Make sure the documents are delivered before the last delivery date.

  5. Following the situation: After sending your documents, follow your credit/burs status via e-Government or from the KYK’s website. If there is any failure or problem, contact KYK to fix the situation.

Things to be careful during the renovation process:

  • Continuity of : The KYK credit or scholarship will continue without interruption throughout your study period. However, it is important not to break up the renewal processes every year.

  • The success situation: While the academic success requirement is not required for students who receive credits, students who receive scholarships may be expected to maintain a certain average of success. It is useful to check the current rules of KYK in this regard.

  • School and ice cream: If you have changed the school or you have frozen your registration, you need to notify the KYK of this situation immediately. Otherwise, your credit/burs can be cut or refund may be requested.

The credit is a repaid support and is offered to a wider student audience. While graduate students can usually receive credits, they may seek stricter criteria for scholarships.

  • Can I apply to KYK without Permesso di Soggiorno? Usually yes. Since your Permesso di Soggiorno may take time to leave, you can handle your affiliate transactions by presenting other documents along with your application certificate or visa. However, you may be asked to add Permesso in the final document presentation to KYK.

  • How long will the loan/bursus be granted? KYK gives master students credits or scholarships throughout the normal study period of the program (usually 2 years). But you need to do renewal processes every year.

Important clues

  • The early application: Applications and processing can be time-consuming. Therefore, take action as early as possible to not miss the last application dates.

  • Communications to: Be in regular contact with both KYK and the Turkish Education Department in Italy. In any issue or uncertainty, contacting the relevant authorities directly allows you to obtain the most accurate information.

  • The document control: Make sure all the documents are complete, up-to-date, accurate and in the desired format. Missing or incorrect documents may cause your application to be rejected.

  • Control of equality: Check your program in Italy in advance. This is a basic requirement for the application.

  • The Financial Planning: Although the KYK credit or scholarship is a significant support, it may not be able to cover all your living and education costs in Italy. Therefore, it is important to make planning for additional financial resources (family support, part-time job opportunities, other scholarships, etc.) especially DIRITO ALLO STUDIO UNIVERSITARY (Diritto allo Studio Universitario) Researching local scholarships in Italy, such as scholarships and regional scholarships, can significantly reduce your financial burden. These burses are usually ISEE (Indicatore della Situazione Economica Equivalente) It is assessed by the document and given according to your family income status. When you are getting a loan, there is no problem with applying for burses like DSU.

Alternatives to Foreign Credit/Burse

The Italian Loan And while the scholarship is a significant financial support for students studying abroad, it’s not the only option. There are also other scholarships and financing options you can benefit from while studying in Italy:

  • The Italian Government: Scholarships granted to foreign students by the Italian Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation (MAECI). It is usually aimed at students at the master and doctoral level.

  • The regional DSU Bursas: Each region of Italy has financial support programs for its own university students. The income is given according to the situation and usually offers a discharge from the study fee, monthly living costs support and accommodation possibility. by ISEE The certificate is the basic criterion for these burses.

  • The Erasmus+ Programme: If you have completed your bachelor’s education in Turkey and are graduating in Italy, you may be able to take advantage of an Erasmus+ internship or learning mobility programmes.

  • The Turkish Education Foundation (TEV) stipends: Various foundations and associations in Turkey, such as TEV, can also offer scholarship opportunities to students who study abroad.

  • Credit of the Bank: Some banks in Turkey offer special education loans to students who will study abroad.

Remember that each financial support program has its own application requirements and processes. Early research and access to accurate information will play a key role in relieving your financial burden.

Don't let financial obstacles blame you while realizing your master's dreams in Italy. With the right steps and a planned approach, The Italian Loan And you can take advantage of other scholarship opportunities to continue your educational life successfully.

What criteria do I need to provide to obtain a bursus?

No, you can’t send it directly. The document you will submit to the KYK, will be this special student certificate approved by Atashelik.

Yes, you do not have any trouble in applying for the regional DSU (Diritto allo Studio Universitario) scholarships in Italy when you get a KYK credit or scholarship. These scholarships are usually assessed according to different criteria (especially the family income status with the ISEE certificate) and do not prevent each other.

Diploma and Transcript Procedures for Master in Italy: Apostolic, Translation and Equivalent Importance

Getting a master's degree in Italy is a prestigious goal that decorates many students' dreams. However, it is important to manage academic and bureaucratic processes properly and fully in order to this goal. At the beginning of these processes Diploma of Italy The documents are being processed. Making your diploma and transcripts acceptable by Italian authorities is the key to successful completion of your application. In this blog post, we will discuss in detail the diploma and transcript processes required for your master's application in Italy, the apostolic, translation, equality processes and the frequently encountered problems.

Diploma Equality Process in Italy: Dichiarazione di Valore

One of the most important steps for foreign students who want to attend higher education in Italy is to document the equivalent of their diplomas and academic records received from abroad with the Italian educational system. This documentation is usually Dichiarazione di Valore (Value Statement) It is provided with a document named.

Dichiarazione di Valore is a document that officially confirms the reward and validity of your diploma and academic history in the Italian educational system. This document is usually requested by universities in Italy and plays a critical role in the assessment of your application. The Value Declaration officially confirms the reality, validity and level of your diploma and transcripts in the Italian education system.

How to get the Dichiarazione di Valore?

This document is usually obtained through the Italian Embassy or Consulates in Turkey. The process usually includes the following steps:

  1. Preparation of the necessary documents: The original status of your diploma and transcripts, apostilled and sworn translation into Italian.

  2. The appointment: Request for a Value Declaration from the Italian representative.

  3. Application and review: Submission of your documents and examination by the consular authorities. In this process, contacting your university can confirm the accuracy of your diploma.

  4. Providing the document: After the review is completed, the Dichiarazione di Valore certificate will be delivered to you.

Since this process can be time-consuming, it is important to start as early as possible taking into account the application dates. One of our students was at risk of missing a visa date because he left the Value Declaration process for the last master. Fortunately, we managed to train the process with a quick action plan.

Apostolic Procedures: Where and How to Do It?

The Apostle is a system of approval that allows the validity of a document to be legally used in another country. This system, which applies between the countries party to the Lahey Convention, applies to Italy as well. Students who want to study in Italy must carry the apostolic charity of their official documents, such as diploma and transcript.

Where is the Apostle?

In Turkey, apostolic procedures are performed by different authorities according to the type of document:

  • Administrative Documents (Diploma and Transcript): The roots or governments.

  • Legal Documents (Justice Registration): Heavy Criminal Court Presidents or Justice Commission Presidents.

For your diploma and transcripts required for your master's applications, you need to apply to the Government of the province where the university you graduate.

How to do Apostles?

  1. The original document: The apostolic procedure is usually done on the original of the document. However, in some cases the apostillus can also be made on the copies of the notary approved "like original". Italian authorities often prefer apostilium made on the original document.

  2. The application: Your document will be requested to the relevant institution (Government/Council) personally or through an authorized person.

  3. Time of processing: The apostolic procedure is usually completed within the same day.

The important note: Before the Apostolic processing, it is useful to confirm from the current requirements of the Italian University or Consulate whether your diploma or transcript will be apostolic on a copy "as original" or on the original. One of our students had a request for additional documents from the university because he did apostillize his copy, which extended the application process.

Diploma and Transcript Translation: The Choice of a Jurious Translator

Universities in Italy, usually documents Italian translation They demand. Even for students applying for English programs, Italian translation may be required in some cases. Therefore, it is very important to manage the translation process properly.

Choice of a sworn translator:

  • Official Approved Translator: The translations must be made by sworn translators accepted by the Italian Consulate or Embassy in Turkey. The list of these translators is usually found on the consulate websites.

  • Truth and Inexactitude: It is critical that the translation is identical to the original document and does not contain any errors. Even the smallest mistake may cause your application to be rejected.

  • The notary approval: The approval of the translation by the notary is also a step that is often required.

The translation of the swear:

  1. Preparing the documents: Prepar your original diploma and transcripts completed by the Apostile process.

  2. Selection of translator: Select a sworn translator from the list specified by the Italian Consulate.

  3. Translation and notary approval: The translator translates your documents into Italian and then these translations are approved by the notary.

These steps ensure that your documents are legally recognized by Italian authorities.

English Diploma Requirements for Translation

This is one of the topics that most confuses students. "My diploma is in English, still I need to translate into Italian?" the question is often asked.

  • The general rule: If the program you’re applying is completely in English and the university clearly indicates, your English diploma and transcript may not be required to be translated into Italian. However, this situation does not apply to every university and every program.

  • To get clear information: It is necessary that you get accurate information about this by contacting the international student office of the university you apply or program coordinators. Some universities, even for English programs Declaration of Valore You can request that the document be translated into Italian.

  • The visa process: At the stage of visa application, the consulates usually require a sworn translation of all documents into Italian. Therefore, even if the university is accepted, a translation in Italian may be required at the visa stage.

One of our students had not translated into Italian, considering that their documents were in English when applying for an English program. However, at the visa date, the Consulate requested the translation of all documents into Italian. This has caused the student to delay his visa application and face additional costs. It will always be wise to choose the safest way to avoid such unexpected situations and make all necessary translations.

Actual as the documents and the status of acceptance

Approved copies of the "original as" which are often used for official documents in Turkey can be evaluated in different ways in the reception processes in Italy.

  • The Apostle: As we mentioned earlier, the apostolic process is usually done on the original document. Although notary-approved copies can also be apostilled, Italian authorities often prefer the apostilled status of original documents.

  • The University Applications: While universities will usually accept scanned copies at the application stage, they will ask for an illustration of apostolic and translated original documents at the registration stage.

  • The visa process: During the visa application, the consulates will want to see original documents and ask for apostolic, translated copies. "It's as true" depends on whether the copies are accepted or not, the current practices of the relevant consulate.

Therefore, it is recommended that you deal with your original documents as much as possible and handle apostolic and translation processes directly through the original documents instead of "as original" copies. This will minimize the potential risks of retardation or delay.

Frequently Asked Questions and Important Tips

Some of the situations and general clues that students who apply for a master's degree in Italy often encounter are:

  • The university portal: Most universities in Italy receive their applications through the Universitaly portal. In this portal, you need to pay attention to the format and size limits when uploading your documents. The documents you upload must contain all the approvals mentioned above (apostile, sworn translation).

  • Right to Study (Right to Study): Most international students studying in Italy have the potential to benefit from the DSU (Diritto allo Studio Universitario) scholarship. For this application. The Paris Parish The document is necessary. ISEE Parificato is an important document that shows the income status of your family and is obtained through consulat in Italy. This document will also require apostolic and Italian sworn translations of your family income documents.   • Management of Time: All of these bureaucratic processes, especially the steps such as apostil, translation, notary approval and Dichiarazione di Valore are time-consuming. Given the University application and visa dates, starting these processes as early as possible will prevent last minute stress and possible delays.

  • Current Information Control: Italy’s visa and education policies may change from time to time. Therefore, it is important that you have the most up-to-date information by regularly checking the websites of the university and the Italian Consulate to apply.

Can I apply to an Italian university without the Dichiarazione di Valore (Value Statement) certificate?

At the application stage, some universities may not apply for Dichiarazione di Valore and may request after admission. However, this document is usually mandatory for the visa application. Therefore, it is most accurate to check the current requirements of the university and visa office you will apply.

If the program you’re applying is completely in English and the university clearly indicates, your English documents may not need to be translated into Italian. However, when applying for a visa, the consulates usually require the sworn translation of all documents into Italian. Therefore, making Italian translation against any possibility is a safer approach.

Italian authorities often prefer apostilium made on the original document. Although noter-approved copies of the "original is" can also be apostilled, it is recommended that processing through the original document in order to avoid possible problems.

How long does the Diploma Equivalent process take for a master's degree in Italy?

In this blog post, we will discuss all the details from searching for accommodation for Turkish students to rental contracts, from selecting a safe area to possible fraud.

Types of Student Accommodation in Italy: Houses, Private Rooms, Apartments

There are a variety of accommodation options available for students in Italy. Each has its own advantages and disadvantages.

Residenze Universitarie (Residenze Universitarie)

University accommodation is the safest and usually the most affordable option, especially for students who first go abroad. Most Italian universities, especially public universities, offer student accommodation within or in which they are agreed.

  • The advantages: They are often located close to the campus, with bills (electricity, water, internet) included in rental, security, socialization facilities and the opportunity to easily communicate with other students. In many countries there are common uses such as workrooms, gyms, washing rooms.

  • The Disadvantages: The content is limited and requires early application. Application processes can usually be complicated and there is no location guarantee. You may not have the chance to choose a room friend and the rules may be more rigorous.

  • The application process: National applications can be made via the university’s websites or along with the DSU (Diritto allo Studio Universitario) scholarship applications. The DSU scholarship is usually aimed at low-income students, and can also include home accommodation.

Apartments in Stanza (Stanza in Appartamento Condiviso)

One of the most common types of student accommodation in Italian cities is renting rooms in shared apartments. This option is ideal for students who are unable to settle in university houses or seek more independence. A few students are gathered together to share the apartment.

  • The advantages: More freedom, the opportunity to experience the local culture closer, usually larger living spaces than home. Location of rooms in Italy The option also offers the opportunity to meet people from different nations and practice language.

  • The Disadvantages: Difficulty in finding a reliable partner, the separate calculation and management of bills, potential problems that may occur with the host.

  • Things to be careful: It is important that you must see the apartment and your room friends before renting, carefully read the rental contract and make a clear agreement on how to pay the invoices.

Apartments in Affitto (Appartamento in Affitto)

Renting a whole apartment alone or with your friends is the option that offers the highest freedom but also the most expensive and requires the highest responsibility. It can be preferable especially for students who come with a group of friends or plan to stay longer.

  • The advantages: Create your own living space completely, the freedom to choose a partner, less interaction with the host.

  • The Disadvantages: High rental fees, the deposit amount, the fact that all of the invoices belong to you, additional costs such as the real estate commission. It can be difficult to find a furnished apartment.

  • Things to be careful: Finding a apartment in big cities can be both time-consuming and expensive. It is important to read all the articles of the rental contract carefully and, if necessary, to get legal support.

In Italy, rental contracts are subject to certain legal frameworks as in Turkey. It is important that you be careful before signing a contract and know your rights.

Types of Contract

  • Contratto di Affitto per Studenti (Student Rental Contract): Such contracts are usually used for short or medium-term rental, ranging from 6 to 36 months. It is common in university cities and may include special provisions for students.

  • Contratto di Locazione ad Uso Abitativo: It applies to longer-term (usually 4+4 years) rental. As a student, signing such a contract should be well considered because it will require long-term commitments.

What to be taken into account

  • The written contract: Always request a written rental contract. Oral agreements are not legal and may lead to problems in the future.

  • The registered contract (Registrato): Registration of the loan contract to the Italian Tax Office (Agenzia delle Entrate) is a legal obligation. A registered contract protects both the owner and the tenant. A non-registered contract is legally invalid and deprives you of legal rights.   • The entrance and exit port (Verbale di Consegna/Riconsegna): Keeping a detailed attachment to the state of the apartment (photo) when moving to and while moving to the apartment will prevent possible disputes during deposit refund.

  • The Code of Taxation (Codice Fiscale): You will need to sign a rental contract in Italy and the tax code (Codice Fiscale) for bills. You can get this code from the tax offices in Italy (Agenzia delle Entrate) or the Italian Consulates.

  • The Convention of the Convention: The terms of termination of the contract (pre-notification period, etc.) must be read carefully. Usually, the rental owner must be informed 3 to 6 months in advance to terminate the contract.

Safety and transportation options

When choosing a place of accommodation, not only the price, but also the safety of the area, the ease of transport to the university and social facilities should be taken into account.

What should I take care of when making a student rental contract in Italy?

Application for Italian Universities: General Review

Italy, with its rooted educational tradition, prestigious universities and cultural wealth, is one of the world’s favorite educational destinations for students. Especially in recent years, with the increase in the number of English programmes, the attraction for students from Turkey and all over the world has increased further. but Italian University Application The process has its own dynamics and bureaucratic stages compared to other European countries. This process can be managed without trouble by taking the right steps and following up-to-date information.

Introduction to the Italian education system, usually consists of two main stages: direct application to universities and then pre-enrollment (pre-enrollment) processes. These two processes are steps that complement each other but are carried out through different platforms. One of the areas where students are most difficult and the potential to make mistakes is the correct understanding and complete completion of these processes. In this blog post, we will discuss the application process for candidates who want to get university education in Italy with all details, especially Universitarian Pre-Register We will step by step explain the use of the portal and present suggestions for solutions to frequent problems. Our goal is to simplify this seemingly complex process and help candidates reach their goals.

Universitaly Portal: Pre-Registration Steps and Document Loading

Licensed in Italy Master Application in Italy Pre-registration processes, which are an integral part of their processes, are carried out through the National Student Portal, Universitaly. This portal allows students to apply to Italian universities through a central system and plays a key role in the arrangement of the "pre-acceptance letter" which is necessary for visa application.

Creating and Applying an Universitaly Account

The universitaly portal is usually opened in November-December of each year, and although the latest dates for pre-registration processes differ between universities, it usually lasts until May-July months. Therefore, it is critical for candidates to follow their application calendar closely.

  1. Creating the account: The first step is to create a personal account on the Universitaly portal. In this stage, the basic personal information (name, surname, date of birth, nationality, etc.) is entered.

  2. University and Program Selection: After creating your account, you will have to choose the university and program you want to apply. In Italy, every student can usually make a single program pre-registration. However, some exceptions or universities may differ in their own internal processes. Therefore, make sure to check the specific guidelines on the university’s website you want to apply.

  3. Supplement of necessary documents: This is the most important and careful part of the process. Documents to be charged to Universitaly are usually:

* Copy of the passport: A color copy of a passport with sufficient validity period. * High School Diploma / University Diploma and Transcript: High school diploma and transkripts for bachelor applications, master diploma and transkripts for applications. These documents are usually requested for Italian sworn translations and apostolic charity. * Certificate of Language Qualification: A language qualification certificate (e.g. a language qualification certificate) according to the educational language of the applicable program (Italian or English). IELTS, TOEFL, CELI and CILS Some universities can also take their own exam. * A Letter of Motivation (A Letter of Motivation): A letter that describes why you chose this program and this university, indicating your personal goals. * Letter of Recommendation (Letter of Recommendation): Recommendation letters from your academics or employers. * Curriculum Vitae (Curriculum Vitae): A resume of your academic and professional history. * DSU (Diritto allo Studio Universitario) Application Certificate: A certificate that indicates that the borrowing and foreign application are made. (These documents may not be mandatory at the application stage, but may be useful for the visa application.)

The important note: All the documents uploaded must be in the specified format and size. Furthermore, it is important that the Italian sworn translations and apostolic charges, along with the original documents, are also prepared to avoid any problems in the visa process. "One of our students had a problem with the system due to the format of documents he uploaded to Universitaly, and had to re-edit the documents. It is important to make the right format in the first time to avoid such delays.

Do not follow the application status

After you have uploaded your documents and sent your application, you can track the status of your application via the Universitaly portal. University officials may request approval or additional document after examining your application. Often for approved applications. “Pre-acceptance letter” or “Letter of eligibility” is arranged. This document is a critical condition for the visa application.

What is Conditional Acceptance and How Does the Post-Procedure Work?

The Italian Universities Conditional acceptance (conditional admission) is a common situation especially for high school graduate students or graduate candidates who have not yet obtained a bachelor's degree. This shows that the university finds the student academically sufficient but is not able to fully accept because it has not yet completed some official documents such as a diploma or language qualification.

The meaning and conditions of conditional acceptance

In the conditional admission letter, it is clearly stated that the student must meet certain requirements. These conditions are usually:

  • Proposal for the Diploma: Submission to the University of Higher Education Diploma or Bachelor's Diploma (for Graduate Applications) until a specific date.

  • The completion of language skills: Provision of the language qualification certificate at the required level in the educational language of the applicable program (Italian or English).

  • Do not pass the entry exam: Successfully passing the entry exam, which is mandatory for some programs (especially medicine, such as architecture).

Conditional acceptance depends on the conditions specified in the letter and in the application announcement of the program; it is not a specific registration guarantee alone. The lack of a diploma, language certificate or other conditions is completed during the period and the accuracy of the documents is assessed by the university. The final admission and registration processes depend on the decision of the relevant university and on the remaining academic/administrative conditions. If the conditions are not fulfilled, the offer may remain invalid. Learn in writing from the university when the documents will be delivered and how the condition will be informed.

Conditional admission after visa and registration process

Separate the conditional acceptance letter, pre-registration confirmation and accurate registration. The candidates who need a visa must also follow the documents and application rules of their university’s Universitaly instructions and authorized Italian representation. The University's positive assessment or Universitaly approval, visa appointment or visa grant guarantee does not constitute; the visa decision is given by a competent representation. Confirm from the representation concerned whether you are subject to conditional acceptance and whether the application is not made and which evidence for the missing graduation certificate has been accepted.

Registration (Matrixation of the Matriculation) Follow the university’s own calendar and the requirements in the letter. Some steps such as a diploma, language qualification, document confirmation or payment may need to be completed before you go to Italy. Don’t assume that you can leave the shortcomings after arrival or record it will be done anywhere in September-October. Get the official confirmation of the university on the removal and completion of the registration.

Diploma Equality (Dichiarazione di Valore) and Alternatives

One of the most important bureaucratic steps for international students who want to get university education in Italy Diploma of Equality The process. Traditionally, this process was carried out with a document known as "Dichiarazione di Valore". In recent years, there have been alternatives.

Dichiarazione di Valore (Value Statement)

Dichiarazione di Valore is a formal document that shows the reward and validity of the diploma in the educational system of the country where the student graduates. This document is prepared by the Italian Consulate or Embassy in the country where the student graduates.

Process and Requirements:

  1. Preparation of documents: Documents such as high school diploma or bachelor diploma and transcript must be taken in Italian sworn translations and apostolic charges.

  2. Application to the Consulate: The documents are presented to the Italian Consulate. The Consulate shall review the documents and organise the Dichiarazione di Valore.

  3. Process and Cost: This process may vary depending on the intensity of the consulates, but it can take several weeks to a few months. Also, a certain fee is required for each document.

Dichiarazione di Valore, in the past, was an integral part of visa applications. But today some universities and consulat can also accept alternatives instead of this document.

Alternatives: CIMEA and Other Identification Documents

The Italian Ministry of Education also accepts recognition documents organized by organizations such as CIMEA (Centro di Informazione sulla Mobilità e le Equivalenze Accademiche) in order to facilitate the diploma equality processes.

  1. CIMEA “Statement of Comparability” and “Statement of Verification”: CIMEA is an organization that evaluates the reward of international diplomas in the Italian educational system and organizes official recognition documents.

* Statement of Comparability: A document that indicates the reward and value of your diploma in the Italian education system. * Statement of Verification: It is a document that confirms the accuracy and originality of your diploma.

These documents can be obtained by online application and usually offer a faster and more practical alternative than Dichiarazione di Valore. It is important to check whether the applicant university accepts CIMEA documents. Most Italian universities and consulates now accept these documents.

  1. Other identification documents: Some universities or programs may carry out their own internal equality assessment processes or other recognition documents with international validity (e.g. Documents obtained from other centres in the ENIC-NARIC network) can be accepted.

The important note: The Diploma Equality process is a critical step that must be completed before you arrive in Italy. Lacked or incorrect documents may prevent you from making your accurate registration to the university. "One of our students" left the last master in the Dichiarazione di Valore process and was hard to reach a visa date. Therefore, it is essential to start this process early and prepare all the documents rigorously.

Date and methods of application results

The completion time for university applications in Italy varies according to the university, program and application period. The rules of the candidates are important to follow this process with patience and regularity.

Calendar of the Results

  • Early application periods: Some universities may open early application periods, especially for English programmes. The results of applications made during these periods are usually explained earlier (for example, between January-March months).

  • Normal application periods: The normal application periods for most universities usually end in spring and the results are usually published between May-July.

  • The delays: Intense or failures in administrative processes may cause delays in the disclosure of the results. Instead of panicing in these cases, it is the best approach to obtain information using the official communication channels of the university.

Methods to follow the results

  1. The University Application Portal: Regularly check the online application portal of the university you apply. Acceptance or rejection letters are usually published through this portal.

  2. The email: The universities also usually report the results of their application by e-mail. Therefore, check the e-mail address you use when applying regularly and don’t forget to review the spam folder as well.

  3. The university portal: You can also find information about the status of your application via the Universitaly portal you have pre-registred. The pre-acceptance letter (pre-acceptance letter) is written through this portal.

  4. Communications Channels of the University: If you don’t get results for a long time or if you think there is a problem, do not hesitate to contact the university’s international student office or related department directly.

The steps after acceptance

After receiving your acceptance letter, you will have to take the following steps:

  • Approval of acceptance: Confirm your admission as required by the University (usually by filling out an online form or sending an email).

  • The visa application: Apply for a student visa to the Italian Consulate along with the admission letter and other necessary documents.

  • Home and Burs Applications: If you haven’t made a scholarship or foreign application or are waiting for the results of the application, it is important to accelerate these processes. especially DIRITO ALLO STUDIO UNIVERSITARY (Diritto allo Studio Universitario) Scholarships are an important source of financial support for international students studying in Italy. ISEE (Indicatore della Situazione Economica Equivalente) The certificate plays a critical role in DSU applications and the determination of university fees. The preparation of this document is also a separate bureaucratic process and must be investigated in advance.

  • Tickets and accommodation: After your visa processes are completed, get your flight ticket and set the place to stay when you arrive in Italy.

Italian University Application The process is a journey that requires rigidity and patience. But with the right guidance and the steps taken in time, it is possible to successfully complete this process. Remember that each university and program may have its own specific requirements, so it will always provide the most accurate information to check the official website of the university you want to apply.

Frequently Asked Questions

I made an error in a document I uploaded to Universitaly, can I fix it?

Yes, usually if you have not yet pressed the "Send" button on the Universitaly portal or if it has not been examined by the university, you will be able to edit or re-upgrade documents. However, it may be more difficult to make changes after your application has been sent and the study has begun and you may need to contact the university. Therefore, it is best to carefully check the documents before charging.

When and how to obtain the ISEE certificate for the DSU scholarship application?

The ISEE certificate is a document that shows the economic status of students in Italy and is used to determine the university fees with the DSU scholarship applications. A special ISEE type is calculated for international students called "ISEE Parificato". This document is usually obtained after arrival in Italy, through specific "CAF" (Centro di Assistenza Fiscale - Tax Assistance Centers) offices or through the institutions where the university has agreed. The process usually starts in September-October and may take a few weeks to complete. DSU scholarship applications are usually open in the summer months and it is important that the ISEE certificate reaches the application dates.

Can I apply for more than one university or program during pre-enrollment?

As a general rule, you can make a preliminary registration of only one program for a semester through the Universitaly portal. However, in some specific cases or universities can differ their own internal processes. For example, some universities may accept multiple program applications through their own direct application portals. Therefore, it is critical that you always check the specific guidelines for the university and program you want to apply.

I have a conditional acceptance but I will not get my diploma until the visa date, what should I do?

First, inform your university about the status and ask in writing whether the admission requirement, the date of end of delivery and the temporary graduation certificate are accepted or not. Please also confirm from the authorized Italian representation that you will accept the same document in terms of visa application. The text to be received from your school will not automatically replace the diploma or requested formal document. Do not assume that the accurate registration has been completed without removing the university requirement; do not assume that the visa will be granted without a representative decision.

Permesso di Soggiorno (Permesso di Soggiorno) Process: Application, renewal and travel rights

Italy is one of the favorite destinations for international students and professionals with its rich culture, rooted educational system and quality of life it offers. But one of the most important bureaucratic processes that everyone who wants to settle in this beautiful country will encounter. Italy residence permit Permesso di Soggiorno. This document is a basic requirement that allows you to legally reside, study or work in Italy. Given the complexity and details of the process, having accurate and complete information is of great importance. In this comprehensive guide, we will step-by-step address the processes of application, renewal and travel rights in Italy. Our goal is to help you complete this process without problems and prepare you for potential challenges that you may face.

Permesso di Soggiorno (Permesso di Soggiorno) Application process step by step

It is a legal obligation to apply for a residence permit within the first 8 business days after entering Italy. Not following this time can lead to serious problems. The application process usually includes the following steps:

  1. Visum and entry to Italy: Before you arrive in Italy, you need to obtain a national (Type D) visa that is suitable for your purposes such as education, work or family unification. This visa is the first step for your legal entry to Italy.

  1. The Kit Postal (Kit Postal) The necessary forms and instructions for the application for a seat permit are usually provided by the Post Office (Ufficio Postale) in a special cover called "Kit Postale". This kit is usually found in the post that offers the "Sportello Amico" service.

  1. Fill out the forms and preparing the necessary documents: The forms inside the kit should be filled carefully and complete. These forms usually include your personal information, your address in Italy, your visa type and the purpose of your application. In addition to the forms, you will need a series of documents that vary depending on your application type.

The necessary documents and the postal processes

Italy residence permit In general, the following documents are required to apply:

  • Passport and Visa Copies: The page containing your personal information of your passport and photocopies of your Italian visa.

  • Photocopies of the visa application documents: Copies of the documents you use in your visa application, such as university admission letter, scholarship certificate, bank account deposit.

  • Health Insurance is: A health insurance policy in Italy (usually one year).

  • The photo: Four biometric photographs.

  • The Tax Pulu (Marca da Bollo): Tax pounds of a certain value that can be supplied from the postal or tobacco (tabaccheria).

  • The application fee: The application fee for Permesso di Soggiorno.

  • Certificate of accommodation: A rental contract that indicates your address in Italy, a country certificate or a declaration that you are a guest (Dichiarazione di Ospitalità).

The Postal Process: When all your documents are ready, you will gradually complete your application to a post offering the "Sportello Amico" service. The post office officer will check that your forms are complete, receive the necessary payments and give you a grant called "Ricevuta". This confirmation is your legal proof that your application has been received and shows your legal status in Italy until your residence permit is issued.

Fingerprint and the following process.

Shortly after receiving your receipt from the mail (usually within a few weeks), The Questura You will be informed by a date and time of the appointment. This date is intended to give fingerprints and check your original documents.

The fingerprint date: What you need to take with you when you go to your date:

  • Recevuta (postal permission)

  • Your passport

  • by Vizen

  • All the original documents you present in your application (university admission letter, scholarship certificate, insurance policy, etc.)

  • Four Biometric Photos

In Questura, the staff will check your documents, take your fingerprints and give you a new date of appointment or tell you that you will receive a SMS informing when your permission card will be ready.

One of our students had to take a date again because he was missing the necessary documents while going to an fingerprint date. This resulted in the prolongation of the process and additional stress. Therefore, it is critical to make sure that all the original documents are with you when you go to your date.

Delivery of the seat permit card: When your admission card is ready, you usually need to gradually deliver it back to Questura. In some cases, it can also be sent by mail. Before receiving your card, make sure the information on it (name, surname, date of birth, type of visa, etc.) is correct. If you have any errors, please notify them immediately.

Travel rights with Permesso Recevuta: Turkey and Schengen Area

until your permission card reaches your hand, provided by the mail The Permesso RicevutaThe (makbuz) proves your legal status in Italy. However, this permission has some restrictions on travel rights:

Travel to Turkey: You can take the Permesso receipt directly to Turkey. But when you return to Italy, you must definitely come to Italy with a direct flight. You may have trouble making a transferable flight through another Schengen country, as these countries may not accept you without a valid visa or entry permit card when entering the Schengen area. Even if you have a valid Schengen visa on your passport, it is the safest way to make a direct flight with the receipt when entering Italy.

Travel in the Schengen Area: Travel within the Schengen area with permesso receipt is legally impossible. It is advised that you do not travel to other Schengen countries until your entry permit card reaches your hand. After your card has been in your hand, you can travel freely to other Schengen countries within 90 days with your Italian residence permit.

One of our students tried to move to France with a permesso receipt and had trouble at the border. He was told he had no right to free movement in the Schengen area before his residence permit was issued and he was forced to return. In order not to face such unwanted situations, it is important that you make your travel plans based on the date of delivery of your entry permit card.

The process of renewal of the seat permission and what to be taken into account

As your stay in Italy extends, you will need to renew your residence permit. The renewal process is similar to the first application process but may show some differences.

Time of renewal: Before the expiry of your permission at least 60 days ago You need to apply for a renewal (in some cases earlier). It is very important to be careful for this time so that you do not stay in an unlawful situation with a full-time residence permit.

The necessary documents (for renewal): The "Kit Postale" for the renewal application is also provided and filled. While the required documents are similar to the first application, some additional documents may be requested:

  • Photo of Permesso di Soggiorno

  • Documents that show your education or work status during your stay in Italy (transcript, employment contract, student certificate, etc.)

  • Current bank accounts that show you have sufficient financial resources

  • Health Insurance Day

  • Certificate of accommodation

  • Tax and application fees

The process: The renewal application is also made by post and then the fingerprint date is received from Questura. The process can usually go faster than the first application, but it may still take a few months to get your card in your hand. In this process, the travel rights and receivuta are applied in the same way.

Frequent Problems and Solutions

1. Don’t miss the appointment:

  • The problem: Missing a fingerprint date from Questura can lead to extension of the process and even rejection of your logging permit.

  • The solution: Check your date notifications (SMS or mail) regularly. If you missed it, contact Questura as soon as possible to explain the situation and request a new date. If necessary, provide a valid excuse (e.g., an emergency) that you have missed the date.

2. Lost or incorrect documents:

  • The problem: The lack of or incorrect submission of documents in the application may cause your application to be rejected or the process with additional document requests can be extended.

  • The solution: Check carefully the full list of necessary documents before making your application. Keep the copies and original documents ready. In cases of doubt, check the Questura website or get support from a consulting company.

3. Long waiting periods:

  • The problem: Italy residence permit The process can take a very long time, especially in the beginning of the educational period. The release of the card can sometimes take more than 6 months.

  • The solution: Make your plans taking into account that the process may be long. Remember that Recevuta is a legal document, but take into account travel restrictions. You can get information by contacting Questura for cases where you need to rush, but usually there is not much that you can do.

4. Change of address:

  • The problem: Change of address after the application has been made may cause your card to be sent to the wrong address or not to reach you.

  • The solution: When you change the address, you must notify Questura of this situation. This is usually done by giving a new "Dichiarazione di Ospitalità" or rental contract.

5. The financial insufficiency:

  • The problem: Especially in renewal applications, the lack of sufficient financial resources to show that you can meet your living costs in Italy may cause your application to be rejected.

  • The solution: Make sure you have enough money on your bank account. If you are getting a burs, update your burs documentation. If you get support from your family, their bank accounts and sponsorship letters may also be useful.

Italy residence permit The process may seem complicated and scary at first glance. But with the right knowledge, careful preparation and patience it is possible to successfully complete this process. Remember that acting in accordance with the law and providing the necessary documents in full at each step is the key to the process's smooth progress. We wish you success in your new life in Italy!

Frequently Asked Questions

1. How long do I have after entering Italy for Permesso di Soggiorno application?

It is a legal obligation to apply for Permesso di Soggiorno within the first 8 business days after entering Italy.

2. Can I go to Turkey with Permesso Ricevuta and return to Italy?

Yes, with Permesso Ricevuta you can go to Turkey and return to Italy. But when you return to Italy, you must come with a direct flight without transfer through another Schengen country.

3. Can I travel to other Schengen countries without my entry permit?

No, traveling to other Schengen countries with Permesso Ricevuta is legally impossible. Your right to free movement in the Schengen area begins after your residence permit has arrived at your hand.

4. When should I apply for a residence permit?

You must apply for renewal at least 60 days before the expiry of your seat permit. It is important to be careful for this time, so that you don’t stay in an unlawful situation.

Health Insurance Requirements for Italian Student Visa

When applying for a student visa to Italy, the documents requested by the Consulate International health insurance. Police is found. This policy is a travel health insurance that is usually valid in the Schengen area and which meets certain minimum guarantees. But there is a significant nuance to be noted here: There may be differences between this insurance made for the visa application and the insurance required for the residence permit after arrival in Italy.

Insurance Policy in the Visa Application Process

The basic requirements for the health insurance policy to be submitted for the visa application are:

  • Duration of validity: The policy must cover the visa requested duration (usually the first few months you plan to enter Italy). In some cases, you may be required to cover the entire visa period. At this point, it is very important to check the current requests of the Consulate.

  • The Schengen Area: The policy should apply not only in Italy, but throughout the Schengen area.

  • The Polish language: It is usually preferable to be in English or Italian. Do not forget to request the English versions of the policy you will receive from Turkish insurance companies.

One of our students erroneously entered the start date of the insurance he made for a visa application and therefore had the risk of refusing his application. Even such simple errors can extend the process, so it is necessary to check the policy details very carefully.

Types and scope of Student Health Insurance in Italy

After settling in Italy, the travel health insurance you usually make for a visa will not be enough. An Italian healthcare system for the application for seating permit (Permesso di Soggiorno) is more comprehensive and consistent with the Italian healthcare system. Italian Health Insurance You need to acquire. The main types of insurance that students can choose in Italy are:

1. Servizio Sanitario Nazionale (SSN) – National Health System Member

SSN is the public health system of Italy and provides a wide healthcare network throughout the country. For students from outside the EU/EEA, membership in SSN is usually possible for a yearly fee.

  • The advantages: It is comprehensive. It welcomes most of the basic health services such as doctor visits, hospital care, medications (with partial payment) and specialized examinations. It allows you to appoint a family doctor (medico di base).

  • The application process: Payment "bollettino" is made from the mail, then the payment deconto and other documents are requested to the local ASL (Azienda Sanitaria Locale) office.

SSN is the most recommended option for students to stay long, as it allows you to have the same rights as Italian citizens and offers the broadest scope.

Some students may prefer private health insurance for reasons such as more flexible dating hours or faster access to certain services. However, an acceptable private insurance policy for a residence permit must meet certain requirements:

  • Duration of validity: Police must cover the time of residence permit. It is usually required for one year.

  • The important note: When making your policy, be sure to know the return conditions in case of a visa refusal.

Usually, partial refund for the unused part of the policy may be possible, but this situation should be specified in your contract.

Italy visa appointment receipt guide: current situation and practical solutions for Istanbul, İzmir, Ankara

The route of many students who dream of studying abroad is Italy with its historical textures, artistic wealth and rooted universities. But one of the first and most critical steps to turn this dream into reality, Italy visa date to take. Due to the intensity and some difficulties in the system in recent periods, this process can be quite devastating for candidates. In this blog post, we will discuss the visa appointment process for students who want to study in Italy with all the details, we will evaluate the current situation in Istanbul, İzmir and Ankara and offer practical solutions to the challenges you may face. Our goal is to make this complex process understandable and managed for you.

Italy Student Visa Date Process Step by Step

The application for Italian student visa is a process that requires careful planning and patience. Knowing all the steps before getting a date will help you accelerate the process.

  1. University Admission and Registration: Obtaining an admission letter from a university in Italy is the basis for the visa application. You cannot apply for a visa without your admission letter. After admission, you may need to complete the university’s registration procedures and make the necessary payments.

  1. University Registration and Pre-Registration: All international students who want to study in Italy must make pre-registration through the Universitaly portal. This portal is a central platform for universities to evaluate applications and organize the admission letter. After the pre-registration processes are completed, you will be expected to receive an admission letter from the university.

  1. Identify the type of visa: Student visa is usually included in the "Type D National Visa" category. This applies to long-term training for more than 90 days. Make sure you choose the right type of visa when applying for a visa.

  1. Preparation of the necessary documents: A broad list of documents is required for the visa application. These documents include a passport, an admission letter, financial qualification proof (bank account deposit, scholarship documents), residence proof, travel health insurance, high school/university diplomas and transcripts, language qualification certificate (if there is) and visa application form. It is important that the documents are complete and up-to-date. especially Financial competence and The accommodation The documents are one of the elements that visa officials most pay attention to.

  1. Accommodation on the IDATA Dating System: The Italian Consulates usually accept visa applications through an intermediary entity named IDATA. The date process is carried out through this platform.

IDATA Dating System: Use Tips and Frequently Asked Questions

The IDATA system can be compelling from time to time due to intensity. Here are the things you need to pay attention when using this system and frequently asked questions:

  • Registration of the system: You need to create an account via the IDATA website. You can log in to the date calendar by logging into this account.

  • Follow the date availability from the current channels of the authorized institution. There is no general guarantee that the container will be opened on a specific day or hour. Protect your application information; do not rely on the promise of accurate results by uncertified intermediaries.

  • to be fast: When the dating slots are opened, they can be closed in a very short time. Therefore, it is important that when you log in to the system and see a suitable date, you quickly confirm it without hesitation.

  • Internet and Internet connection: Using a strong and stable internet connection reduces the risk of system collapse while getting a date. Also, you can try different browsers (Chrome, Firefox, Edge) to see which system works better.

  • No warning of “no date”: If you see the constant "No Dating" warning on the site, this means that all existing slots are filled or the system has not yet opened new slots. Do not give up and continue to check again at different times.

Calling for calls and things to be careful

Candidates who have difficulty finding a date through the IDATA website often try their chances by phone. But that also brings difficulties in itself.

  • Intensive telephone lines: IDATA call center is experiencing excessive intensity, especially during dating periods. It is quite common to face situations such as waiting for a long time or falling the line.

  • Testing at different times: Calling to the call center at different hours of the day, especially near the start or end of the job, can even increase your chances of connecting. One of our students said they noticed that there was less intensity during the lunch holidays.

  • Get the correct information: When you talk by phone, it may not always be possible to get clear information about when the system will open or the date status. In some cases, there may be contradictions between the information on the website and the information provided by phone. Therefore, it is useful to follow both the website and the phone line at the same time.

  • Be patient and try again: Taking a date by phone is a process that requires patience and re-experience. Don’t give up even if you fail in the first attempt.

Istanbul, Izmir, Ankara's current date situation

The Consulates of Italy in Turkey (Istanbul, Ankara) and the Honorary Consulates (Izmir) serve through different visa application centers. Each city has its own dynamics.

  • of Istanbul: Italy’s largest consulate is located in Istanbul and the vast majority of student visa applications are made from here. So, in Istanbul Italy visa date Find it may be one of the most difficult processes. The dating calendar is expanding quickly and a limited number of new slots are opened. Especially in the summer, when university applications and admission periods are concentrated, the situation is even worse.

  • and Ankara: The Italian Embassy in Ankara can usually be less intense than Istanbul, but there is also time to time to find a date. The candidates to apply from Ankara are also important to monitor the system regularly and move quickly.

  • by Izmir: The honorary consulate in Izmir can accept applications for certain types of visas but long-term visas, such as student visa, can usually be directed to Istanbul or Ankara. Ismael visa date It is most accurate to obtain the latest information about the situation from the IDATA website or the relevant consulate. In some cases, it may be necessary to provide certain conditions to apply from Izmir.

In general, the main problem with finding a date in all cities is that opened slots remain insufficient to meet the demand. This situation clearly indicates that students should not leave the visa application process to the last minute.

Alternative solutions for those who don’t find a date

There are some alternative solutions for candidates who experience serious difficulties in finding a date:

  1. Different Consulate Regions: It is essential to apply to the consulate in which your residence is connected. However, in certain specific cases or depending on the intensity of the consulties, it may be useful to consult with the relevant consulate whether it is possible to apply from a different consulate. But this is quite exceptional and on the initiative of the Consulate.

  2. Request for emergency: In very rare cases, if you have an urgent and documentable reason (e.g., if your university’s registration dates are too close and no other appointment), you can request an emergency appointment directly to the consulate by e-mail. The probability of acceptance of this request is low, but it may be worth trying. Do not forget to add all the documents that support your request (acceptance letter, date of registration, screenshots showing you have not received a date, etc.)

  3. Visa Advisory Companies: Professional visa consulting companies like CliniGA can follow this process on your behalf and support you in getting a date. Experienced consultants can increase your chances of finding a date because they are more familiar with the system's functioning. They can also make your application progress more smooth by preventing possible errors in the document preparation and application process.

The necessary documents and preparation process for the visa application

After the visa appointment has been obtained, the most important step is to prepare a complete and accurate application file.

  • The passport: A passport with a validity of at least 6 months and 2 empty pages.

  • Form of visa application: Full and signed visa application form.

  • The Biometric Photo: Biometric photographs in accordance with the passport standards.

  • Letter of acceptance: Original admission letter from the university in Italy.

  • Proof of accommodation: Proof of your first stay in Italy (at least 1 month) (hotel reservation, homeland certificate, rental contract, etc.). If your stay is not yet confirmed, you can start with the first few weeks of hotel reservation.

  • Certificate of Language Qualification: Depending on the program you apply (Italian or English), a document that shows your language qualification (e.g. IELTS, TOEFL, CILS, CELI).

  • Study Documents : High school diploma and transcript (along with apostolic and swearing translation). If you apply for a post-university master's degree, your university diploma and transcription are also required.

  • The Letter of Intent: A letter of intention that explains why you want to get this education in Italy, highlighting your academic goals and your interest in Italy.

  • and the CV (CV): A current CV that summarizes your academic and professional history.

  • Ticket reservation: Reserve a flight ticket (not recommended to take a certain ticket without the visa confirmation).

It is important that all the documents are presented together with their original and photocopies, and that their sweeping translations have been made. The Consulate has the right to request additional documents. The ISEE certificate (Equivalent economic situation indicator) The DSU Bursas Applications, apart from the visa process but have critical importance in terms of living costs and scholarship opportunities in Italy. These documents are usually not required during the visa application but are required for student discounts and scholarships after you go to Italy.

You can successfully complete this process with the right knowledge, patience and professional support when needed. Remember, starting early and following all steps carefully will reduce your stress and increase your chances of success.

Frequently Asked Questions

When does the Italian student visa dates open?

There is no specific and fixed opening time or day for Italian student visa dates. It is usually observed that new slots can be opened at midnight or early in the morning. It is recommended that candidates check the IDATA system regularly and at different times.

I get the "No Dating" warning in the IDATA system, what should I do?

The "No Dating" warning means that all existing dating slots are filled or the system has not yet opened new slots. In this case, don’t give up, continue to check the system again on different days and hours, especially late at night or early in the morning.

Can I get a visa appointment from a different consulate than the city I reside in?

Visum applications must usually be made from the consulate area where your residence is connected. But in exceptional cases and on the initiative of the Consulate, application from a different city may be possible. You can obtain the most accurate information by contacting the visa department of the consulate or IDATA call center.
